Following , we use a fine-grained human evaluation protocol which requires the annotators to identify different types of span-level coherence errors in the summaries. We adopted the taxonomy of coherence errors proposed by  and modified it for GovReport, which results in four types of coherence errors... (1) Missing Information/Reference about an Event/Object (RefE)... (2) Abrupt Transition from the Previous Topic (TopicE)... (3) Inconsistent, Conflicting Information (InconE)... (4) Repetition (RepE).

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. The paper focuses on abstractive text summarization with a novel locality-based approach. It uses standard ROUGE metrics for automatic evaluation and conducts detailed human evaluation for coherence. No LLM-as-judge evaluation is used. The main normalization needed was simplifying ROUGE variants and consolidating the human evaluation criteria.
